idea:
# Neighborhood clinic
A small internal-medicine clinic runs its day on one shared system: bookings, reception, the patient interview,
the doctor's notes, prescriptions, billing, medicine stock and waiting-time estimates. The reception tablet, the
doctor's PC, the stock screen, the patient's phone and the waiting-room display each have their own screen.
Language: English.

## Data
- Patients: name, age, chronic conditions, allergies, phone. Start with 8 believable patients.
- Bookings: patient, time, purpose, status (booked / arrived / cancelled). Start with 6 bookings for today.
- Reception: number, patient, time, symptom in a few words, urgency (high / medium / low), status (waiting / interviewed / with doctor / to pay / done), minutes waited.
- Interviews: reception number, summary, points to watch, note for the doctor.
- Exam records: reception number, doctor's note, assessment, draft prescription, next visit.
- Prescriptions: reception number, medicine, dose, days, interaction warning.
- Stock: medicine, left, minimum, on order. Start with 12 medicines.
- Bills: reception number, amount, breakdown, paid.
- Waiting-room notice: the number being called, the expected wait and one line of guidance.
- Today's summary: check-ins, patients seen, average wait, anything worth attention, in one sentence.
- Clock: the current time, starting at 9:00.

## Screens
- Reception (tablet): the notice; patient name and symptom inputs with a "Check in" button; today's bookings with
  "Arrived" and "Cancel" on each; reception list, most urgent first, with urgency, status, minutes waited and
  "To billing"; bills waiting with "Paid"; a "Next 10 minutes" button.
- Consulting room (PC): who is with the doctor; the waiting list, most urgent first, with "Call in"; interviews;
  the doctor's note input with "Record exam"; exam records with "Prescribe"; prescriptions.
- Stock (PC): medicines with left, minimum, on order and "Order"; today's summary.
- Patient (phone): "Your turn" with the notice; reception number and a longer description of symptoms with
  "Send interview".
- Waiting room (display): the notice in large type, and the waiting numbers with minutes waited.

## Behaviour
- Check in: create the reception entry (next number, the clock time, waiting); judge urgency from the symptom and
  the patient's conditions and age; mark today's booking for that patient as arrived; estimate the wait from who is
  waiting and how urgent they are; rewrite the notice.
- Arrived: mark the booking arrived and check that patient in the same way. Cancel: mark it cancelled.
- Send interview: summarise the description, write points to watch and a note for the doctor, mark the entry
  interviewed and revise its urgency if the answers warrant it.
- Call in: put the chosen entry with the doctor, move anyone already with the doctor to "to pay", update the notice.
- Record exam: from the doctor's note and the interview, write the assessment, a draft prescription and the next visit.
- Prescribe: turn the draft into prescriptions, check allergies, conditions and interactions and write warnings;
  reduce stock and put anything below its minimum on order.
- To billing: estimate the amount and breakdown from the exam and prescriptions. Paid: mark the bill paid and the
  entry done, and rewrite today's summary.
- Next 10 minutes: move the clock on 10 minutes, add 10 to everyone's minutes waited, sometimes add a believable
  walk-in patient, rewrite the notice and the summary.
- Order: put the medicine on order.

## Checks
- Checking in "Ken Sato" with "chest tightness" gives high urgency and puts him at the top of the list.
- Sending an interview adds one interview and marks that entry interviewed.
- Calling in, recording the exam and prescribing adds prescriptions and reduces the stock used.
- Billing and paying marks the entry done and rewrites today's summary.

start.name: Neighborhood Clinic
start.brief:
One shared system for a small internal-medicine clinic. Collections: patients, bookings, reception, interviews, exams, prescriptions, stock, bills, notice (single item), summary (single item); value clock (starts 9:00).
Intent rules:
- Check in (inputs patient name, symptom): add reception entry with next number, clock time, status waiting, minutes waited 0. Judge urgency from symptom, patient's chronic conditions and age (chest tightness/pain, breathing trouble, fainting = high; fever, pain in older/chronic patients = medium; mild cold, refill = low). Mark that patient's booked booking arrived. Estimate wait from waiting people and urgency; rewrite notice (number called, expected wait, one line of guidance). Unknown names: add a new patient minimally.
- Arrived: mark booking arrived and check in the same way using the booking purpose as symptom. Cancel: mark cancelled.
- Send interview (reception number, description): add interview with summary, points to watch, note for doctor; set entry status interviewed; raise/lower urgency if warranted.
- Call in (chosen entry): set it to with doctor; anyone already with doctor becomes to pay; update notice and the "with doctor" value.
- Record exam (doctor's note): add exam record for the entry with assessment, draft prescription, next visit, using note and interview.
- Prescribe (exam record): create prescription rows (medicine, dose, days), check allergies, conditions, interactions, write warning (or "none"); reduce stock by plausible amounts; if left < minimum set on order.
- To billing: set entry to to pay if not; add bill with estimated amount (consultation about 1,500 yen-style or $ amounts, use USD) and breakdown from exam and prescriptions, paid false.
- Paid: bill paid, entry done, rewrite summary (check-ins, seen, average wait, attention point in one sentence).
- Next 10 minutes: clock +10, every non-done entry minutes waited +10, sometimes add a believable walk-in, rewrite notice and summary.
- Order: set stock on order (add reorder quantity) for the medicine.
Always keep the notice and summary current.
